safety_line: Can spread dengue, Zika, and chikungunya locally. See a doctor if you develop fever, rash, or joint pain after being bitten.
traits: Bites in daytime, especially ankles and elbows
Black with white scales forming a lyre (violin) shape on top of the thorax
Breeds in bottle-cap amounts of standing water around the home

look_alikes.difference: Yellow fever mosquito has a lyre-shaped mark on the thorax; Asian tiger mosquito has a single straight white stripe down the center of the back.
look_alikes.next_photo: A close-up of the back (thorax) while it rests on skin or a wall.

copy.what_it_means: It doesn't need a pond — a plant saucer after one afternoon storm can raise a generation in about a week. Day-biting around the patio suggests container breeding somewhere within a few hundred feet; tipping out standing water is the first, highest-value step, and a technician can evaluate what else is needed.
copy.fact: It doesn't need a pond — a plant saucer after one afternoon storm raises a generation in about a week.
copy.blurb: Southwest Florida mosquitoes breed in as little as a bottle-cap of standing water. Tipping out standing water around the property is the first, highest-value step; a technician can evaluate the rest.

tech_notes: Barrier/larvicide program per protocol. Walk property for container breeding, bromeliads, drains, plant saucers.

safety_line: Capable of spreading dengue, chikungunya, and other viruses. See a doctor if you develop fever, rash, or joint pain after being bitten.
traits: A single bold white stripe down the center of the back
Black legs with white banding on each segment
Aggressive daytime biter, peaking early morning and late afternoon
Same container-breeding habit as the yellow fever mosquito

look_alikes.difference: Asian tiger mosquito has one straight white stripe down the back; yellow fever mosquito has a lyre-shaped mark instead.
look_alikes.next_photo: A close-up of the back (thorax) while it rests on skin or a wall.

copy.what_it_means: This species arrived in the US in used tire shipments in the 1980s and is now established statewide. Same starting point as its cousin: eliminate standing water around the home first; a technician can then treat resting areas for the adults that remain.
copy.fact: It arrived in the US in the 1980s in shipments of used tires — one of the world’s most-traveled mosquitoes.
copy.blurb: Same starting point: eliminate standing water, then a technician can treat resting areas.

tech_notes: Barrier program per protocol. Walk property for tires, containers, bromeliads, tarps holding water.
